Finding gamma-ray pulsars a million times faster

International team discovers previously missed pulsar in data from NASA’s Fermi satellite using algorithms from cryptographic research

https://www.aei.mpg.de/1483164/finding-gamma-ray-pulsars-a-million-times-faster

Using algorithms from cryptography, the new data analysis method is about a million times faster than those used previously. It discovered a pulsar that previous state-of-the-art methods failed to detect.

The pulsar PSR J1622-7204 spins 261 times per second. The scientists identified it using just about 16,000 photons detected by the Fermi Gamma-ray Telescope over a period of approximately 15 years.

The researchers expect that, using the new method and the distributed volunteer computing project @einsteinathome they will be able to find gamma-ray pulsars in binary systems that have hitherto been almost impossible to detect.
